decisions.reason: As a two-component resin injection unit, it remains close to the firm's plural-component and injection knowledge, so management is more likely to retain and refine it, although its niche position and weaker recent visibility raise some rationalization risk.

This resin injection unit also builds on the firm's core fluid-handling and injection capabilities, but possible overlap with neighboring offerings and limited recent visibility make withdrawal somewhat more plausible than for the core spray-gun products.

An automatic airless spray gun is still strongly related to the firm's long-established spray-application competence, so management would usually keep and incrementally improve it rather than exit absent clear failure signals.
A manual airless spray gun sits at the center of the firm's product, service and installed-base knowledge, making continued commercialization the likely choice.

This air-assisted airless spray-gun line leverages deep existing know-how and channel support across several customer segments, so the firm is likely to keep the line and adjust models rather than drop it outright.
